FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A02
Speeding points step up by band: 6 to 10 mph over earns two points, 11 to 15 mph over earns three, and 16 mph or more over earns four. [A02]
Why it matters: group points; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec04-F15, sec04-F16, sec04-F17 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A02
Refusing a chemical alcohol test carries six points, while a driver under 21 refusing a Preliminary Breath Test gets two points. [A02]
Why it matters: group points; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec04-F13, sec04-F17 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A02
Operating while intoxicated is a six-point violation, while impaired driving and any bodily alcohol under 21 are four-point violations. [A02]
Why it matters: group points; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec04-F12, sec04-F15 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A02
Simply failing to yield to emergency vehicles costs two points, but a failure to yield that kills or injures an emergency responder costs six. [A02]
Why it matters: group points; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec04-F14, sec04-F17 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A02
Points on your state driving record are not the same as the points an insurer uses for your rate. [A02]
Why it matters: group points; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec04-F10 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A01
Points drop off after two years, but the convictions behind them stay on the record for at least seven years, some for at least 10, and fatal or impaired driving convictions forever. [A01]
Why it matters: group record; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec04-F04, sec04-F08 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A01
A reexamination is triggered by six or more one-point violations or by 12 or more points, each measured within two years. [A01]
Why it matters: group record; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec04-F09 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A03
A first drug offense means a six-month suspension with no restricted license for 30 days, while a repeat within seven years means one year with none for 60 days. [A03]
Why it matters: group drugs; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec04-F25, sec04-F26 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A03
Carrying up to 2.5 ounces of marijuana is legal for adults 21 or older, yet driving under its influence carries the same penalties as drunk driving. [A03]
Why it matters: group drugs; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec04-F29, sec04-F34 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A03
Coffee, a cold shower, exercise or fresh air may feel sobering, but time is the only thing that removes alcohol’s effects. [A03]
Why it matters: group alcohol; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec04-F21 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A04
Ordinary drivers face reexamination at 12 points or three crashes in two years, while probationary and GDL drivers may be called in after one or two violations. [A04]
Why it matters: group reexam; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec04-F36, sec04-F39 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0030]
